chunks: And Ibn Abī Yaʿfūr narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: A man becomes junub in the Month of Ramadan, then wakes up, then sleeps, then wakes up, then sleeps until morning.
He said: He completes his fast and makes up another day. But if he did not wake up until morning, he completes his fast and it is valid for him.

key_terms.جَازَ لَهُ: it is valid and acceptable for him
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the Month of Ramadan, the month of obligatory sawm
key_terms.يَسْتَيْقِظُ: he wakes up from sleep during the night
key_terms.يَقْضِي يَوْماً آخَرَ: he must make up another day in compensation
key_terms.يُتِمُّ صَوْمَهُ: he completes his fast for that day
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: to become junub, entering a state requiring ghusl

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting if someone remains junub until morning in Ramadan after waking and sleeping again?
ai.summary: This hadith explains a fasting ruling for a person who remains in janabah during the night of Ramadan and repeatedly wakes up before dawn but goes back to sleep until morning. If he had awakened and then slept again until dawn, he completes the fast but must make up that day; however, if he did not wake up at all until morning, his fast remains valid.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1898 - Ibn Abi Ya'fur narrated from Abu Abdullah (as):
"I asked him about a man who becomes junub (in a state of ritual impurity) during the Month of Ramadan, wakes up, then sleeps again, wakes up, and then sleeps again until morning.
Imam (as) said: 'He should complete his fast but must make up another day. However, if he does not wake up until morning, he may complete his fast, and it is valid for him.'"
